title: Aircall vs Unitel Voice — Jon Martin

description: Aircall and Unitel Voice compared for very small teams: entry prices, cost for three people, minimums and guarantees, and HubSpot call logging.

blocks.html: This comparison is for a founder, a consultant, or a team of up to three who want a business phone number that isn't someone's cell, and are weighing Aircall against Unitel Voice.

These two tools solve different problems. One is a calling platform built to sit inside a CRM like HubSpot. The other is a virtual phone system that gives a small business a main number, extensions, and routing for very little money.

Choose Unitel Voice if you need a professional number and call routing and don't need calls in a CRM. Choose Aircall if every call should land on the HubSpot record and the team will grow into a sales or support line.
For three people, Aircall Essentials comes to about $90 a month on annual billing. Unitel Voice Office is $29.99 per month, or $252 billed yearly (3 users included).

Aircall Essentials is $30 per license per month, billed annually, and Professional is $50 per license per month. There's a minimum of 3 licenses on Essentials and Professional, and you get 25% off for paying annually. Power Dialer comes with Professional.

Aircall logs calls and SMS to HubSpot Contacts, Companies, Deals, and Tickets, with recordings, comments, outcomes, and transcription. Per Aircall, all plans include 250+ integrations, HubSpot among them.

Unitel Voice Solo is $9.99 per month, or $84 billed yearly (1 user). Team is $19.99 per month, or $168 billed yearly (unlimited users). Office is $29.99 per month, or $252 billed yearly (3 users included), with $7.99 per extra user per month.
Unitel Voice offers a 30-day money-back guarantee. Recording isn't included by default: call recording is an add-on at $4.99 per month for the whole team.
If you're one person who needs a main line that rings your cell, Unitel Voice's Solo plan is built for that and costs a fraction of a calling platform.
If two or three people make sales calls and you want notes, recordings, and outcomes on the HubSpot contact, Aircall's HubSpot logging is the reason to pay more.
Aircall's three-license minimum makes it expensive for a solo founder, and the price climbs quickly past Essentials.
Unitel Voice doesn't list a HubSpot integration on the facts checked here, so calls won't land on CRM records by themselves, and recording is an add-on.
Ask whether calls are a sales channel or simply how customers reach you. If they're a sales channel, buy the tool that logs to HubSpot. If not, buy the cheap, reliable line.
Both have a way to back out: Aircall bills monthly if you skip the annual discount, and Unitel Voice has a money-back window.
